title: Standards and assurance register for the OKF ONS metadata bundle

assuranceBoundary.statement: The register records source evidence and tests the bundle's metadata mappings. It does not certify an ONS statistical product, observation, methodology or producer.
assuranceBoundary.absenceRule: Missing source evidence is recorded as not-evidenced, never as non-compliance.
assuranceBoundary.separationRule: Bundle profile alignment and source-product evidence are separate claims with separate status vocabularies.

rules: Observed claims require a retrievable source evidence URL and retrieval metadata.
Inferred claims must state the deterministic inference and may not be presented as producer assertion.
Conflicted claims preserve every material source and identify the conflict.
Stale claims preserve the earlier evidence and the freshness rule that failed.
Not-evidenced is not a finding of non-compliance or inaccuracy.
Profile status describes the OKF mapping only and never confers accreditation or certification.

categories.binding-legislation: Legislation whose applicability is determined by law and context.
categories.statutory-code: The Code of Practice for Statistics made under statutory authority.
categories.official-standard: A current government functional, data or analytical standard.
categories.official-guidance: Official producer, regulator or government guidance and policy.
categories.international-standard: A formally maintained international statistical or ISO standard.
categories.technical-recommendation: A maintained web, semantic or catalogue specification, with its normative status recorded.

standards.title: Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007

applicability.scope: UK Statistics Authority and official-statistics functions governed by the Act
applicability.conditions: Apply the relevant provisions according to the producer and information involved.
applicability.exclusions: The bundle does not interpret legal compliance.

requirements.statement: Preserve evidence of applicable definitions, methodologies, classifications, standards and Code status.
requirements.applicability: Official-statistics metadata where the source publishes this evidence.
requirements.evaluation: Check that every claim retains its official source and that unsupported legal conclusions are absent.

requirements.statement: Do not disclose protected personal information through the metadata bundle.
requirements.applicability: All acquisition, normalisation and publication stages.
requirements.evaluation: Secret and personal-data lint; confirm the bundle contains metadata only.

uiTreatments: Display the sourced statistical status without implying legal endorsement.
Keep confidentiality and access constraints next to access links.
automatedChecks: Reject observations, credentials and request-specific personal information.
Require source URLs for legal or Code claims.

standards.title: Public Sector Bodies (Websites and Mobile Applications) Accessibility Regulations 2018

applicability.scope: Public-sector web and mobile services within the Regulations
applicability.conditions: Service owner must determine legal applicability and exemptions.
applicability.exclusions: The register is not an accessibility audit certificate.

requirements.statement: The demonstrator should meet WCAG 2.2 level AA and publish an accurate accessibility statement.
requirements.applicability: OKF Explorer and published supporting pages.
requirements.evaluation: Automated WCAG checks plus keyboard, zoom, focus, contrast and screen-reader journeys.

uiTreatments: Provide a keyboard-accessible table alternative for every map.
Expose an accessibility statement from every published page.
automatedChecks: Run axe against representative routes.
Test keyboard-only use and 200 percent and 400 percent zoom.

standards.title: Data Protection Act 2018

applicability.scope: Processing of personal data during acquisition and publication
applicability.conditions: Apply where a metadata field contains personal data.
applicability.exclusions: Public organisational contact points are preferred over personal contacts.

requirements.statement: Collect and publish only personal information necessary for the metadata purpose.
requirements.applicability: Contacts, provenance and acquisition logs.
requirements.evaluation: Scan public output for secrets, cookies, request identifiers and unnecessary personal contacts.

uiTreatments: Prefer organisational contact labels and addresses.
automatedChecks: Run secret and personal-data heuristics over generated output.

standards.title: INSPIRE Regulations 2009

applicability.scope: Spatial datasets and services within the Regulations
applicability.conditions: Apply only after an explicit in-scope determination.
applicability.exclusions: Do not mark every dataset with a geographic dimension as INSPIRE.

requirements.statement: Preserve the published GEMINI or INSPIRE discovery record and validation evidence for an in-scope spatial asset.
requirements.applicability: Records explicitly identified as INSPIRE or assessed as in scope.
requirements.evaluation: Validate supplied GEMINI or ISO 19139 metadata without inferring legal scope.

uiTreatments: Show INSPIRE status only when source evidence exists.
automatedChecks: Run the applicable GEMINI validation on supplied metadata.
Require an explicit applicability decision before reporting alignment.

standards.title: Code of Practice for Statistics 3.0: Standards for Official Statistics

applicability.scope: Official statistics and producers subject to the Code
applicability.conditions: Map source evidence to the ten current Standards for Official Statistics.
applicability.exclusions: Do not use superseded Code 2.1 Q1, Q2 and Q3 labels as current requirements.

requirements.statement: Preserve release timing, official-statistics status, revisions and corrections with their nature, scale and explanation.
requirements.applicability: All statistical releases and dataset versions for which evidence is available.
requirements.evaluation: Check release dates and version-chain integrity; distinguish revisions from corrections.

requirements.statement: Preserve source changes and biases, reuse and linkage, recognised classifications, validation against relevant sources, and evidence about error or uncertainty.
requirements.applicability: Statistical products where the producer publishes source, method or validation evidence.
requirements.evaluation: Cross-reference catalogue, release, QMI and methodology evidence; retain conflicts instead of overwriting them.

requirements.statement: Explain consistency over time and comparability across and within geographies, including deviations from recognised definitions or classifications.
requirements.applicability: Series, editions, geographies and related statistical products.
requirements.evaluation: Check that a confusable or related record exposes at least one material discriminator.

requirements.statement: Make quality, uncertainty, sources, methods, representativeness, comparability, limitations and planned changes prominent.
requirements.applicability: Every discovery record, with not-evidenced used where the source is silent.
requirements.evaluation: Measure evidence coverage by field and requirement; do not infer statistical accuracy.

requirements.theme: Accessible, related, reusable and persistent statistics
requirements.statement: Provide accessible outputs, comparisons and related statistics, reusable metadata and persistent archived access.
requirements.applicability: Public bundle records and Explorer routes.
requirements.evaluation: Check links, persistence, accessible presentation and related-product relationships.

uiTreatments: Show official, accredited and development status prominently and exactly as sourced.
Place limitations, uncertainty and revision notices before execution.
Provide Compare alternatives and Related statistics views.
automatedChecks: Reject legacy Q1, Q2 and Q3 labels as the current Code structure.
Evaluate source-backed requirement coverage without emitting a compliance verdict.
Validate revision chains and related-record links.

standards.title: Code of Practice for Statistics 3.0: Standards for Public Use
standards.normativeStatus: Current Code standards replacing the 2022 intelligent-transparency guidance in May 2026

applicability.scope: Public use of statistics, data and wider analysis
applicability.conditions: Apply to explanatory content and generated citations in the demonstrator.
applicability.exclusions: Do not present the replaced 2022 regulatory guidance as current.

requirements.statement: Statistics or data used publicly should be publicly available in a timely way and use the latest reliable source.
requirements.applicability: Public explanations, comparisons and demonstrations.
requirements.evaluation: Check that citations resolve and warn when a selected version is superseded.

requirements.statement: Present statistics with integrity, clarity, context, limitations and source citations, without cherry-picking or undue certainty.
requirements.applicability: Human- and agent-facing summaries.
requirements.evaluation: Require citations for generated factual claims and prohibit unsupported certainty.

requirements.statement: Support impartial expert interpretation and responsible leadership in public use.
requirements.applicability: Interpretive and decision-support features.
requirements.evaluation: Keep generated interpretation distinct from producer evidence.

uiTreatments: Offer a copyable citation with source, version and access date.
Warn clearly about superseded or development data.
automatedChecks: Check source-link health and current-version relationships.
Label generated summaries separately from quoted producer evidence.

standards.title: ONS Quality and Methodology Information
standards.normativeStatus: Official ONS quality and methodology guidance

applicability.scope: ONS statistical products with a QMI or equivalent quality report
applicability.conditions: Populate only from a linked producer source.
applicability.exclusions: A missing QMI link is not proof that no quality work exists.

requirements.statement: Preserve strengths, limitations, methods and evidence for relevance, accuracy, timeliness and punctuality, accessibility and clarity, and coherence and comparability.
requirements.applicability: Products with QMI or equivalent evidence.
requirements.evaluation: Report coverage by dimension; never convert metadata presence into an accuracy score.

uiTreatments: Provide a Quality and methodology view with source-attributed dimension summaries.
automatedChecks: Check QMI link health and source digest.
Use not-evidenced for absent dimensions.

standards.title: ONS Guide to Statistical Revisions
standards.normativeStatus: Official ONS revisions and corrections policy

applicability.scope: ONS dataset editions, versions, releases, revisions and corrections
applicability.conditions: Use the producer's classification where supplied.
applicability.exclusions: Do not infer correction from any changed metadata value.

requirements.statement: Distinguish a quality-improving revision from a correction of a mistake and preserve nature, reason and timing.
requirements.applicability: Version and release records with change evidence.
requirements.evaluation: Validate a single current version, acyclic succession and an explanation for classified changes.

uiTreatments: Show a revision timeline and correction notices adjacent to the selected version.
automatedChecks: Validate version-chain direction and dates.
Flag an unexplained changed version as not-evidenced rather than a correction.

standards.title: Administrative Data Quality Assurance Toolkit

applicability.scope: Official statistics produced from administrative data
applicability.conditions: Assurance is proportionate to data-quality risk and public interest.
applicability.exclusions: Do not infer an A0 to A3 assurance level from catalogue metadata.

requirements.statement: Preserve evidence for operational context and collection, supplier communication, supplier quality checks, and the producer's investigations and documentation.
requirements.applicability: Products whose published methodology identifies administrative sources.
requirements.evaluation: Show four-area coverage and source any assurance level and rationale directly.

uiTreatments: Present a four-area evidence matrix for administrative-data products.
automatedChecks: Require direct source evidence before displaying an assurance level.

standards.title: Government Functional Standard GovS 010: Analysis
standards.normativeStatus: Current government functional standard, updated August 2025

applicability.scope: Government analysis and analytical products
applicability.conditions: The source text distinguishes mandatory shall from advisory should.
applicability.exclusions: Do not upgrade advisory practices to mandatory requirements.

requirements.statement: Analysis should use fit-for-purpose inputs and methods, be repeatable and documented, and retain proportionate assurance, assumptions, uncertainty, limitations and references.
requirements.applicability: Bundle construction and source-published analytical evidence.
requirements.evaluation: Require build provenance and report source-published assurance without treating it as bundle certification.

uiTreatments: Keep source assurance statements, assumptions and limitations together.
automatedChecks: Check deterministic build provenance and evidence URLs.
Keep mandatory and advisory requirement levels machine-readable.

standards.title: The Aqua Book: guidance on producing quality analysis for government

applicability.scope: Government analysis and analytical models
applicability.conditions: Assurance should be independent and proportionate to risk and complexity.
applicability.exclusions: The bundle cannot validate an upstream statistical calculation without observations and method execution.

requirements.statement: Analysis shall be assured through lifecycle QA, verification that it was built correctly, validation that it addresses the right purpose, and documented decisions and uncertainty.
requirements.applicability: OKF build and any source-published analytical assurance.
requirements.evaluation: Report verification and validation separately and reconcile generated metadata to frozen source evidence.

uiTreatments: Separate verification evidence from validation evidence.
automatedChecks: Run independent source-to-bundle reconciliation.
Do not produce a single opaque quality score.

standards.title: Reproducible Analytical Pipelines Strategy

applicability.scope: The metadata acquisition, reconciliation, build and evaluation pipeline
applicability.conditions: Apply proportionately to a metadata-only demonstrator and subsequent publication pipeline.
applicability.exclusions: Live acquisition is separate from deterministic frozen publication.

requirements.statement: Minimise and document manual steps; use open-source tools, peer review, version control, QA and version-controlled documentation.
requirements.applicability: All checked-in build and evaluation workflows.
requirements.evaluation: Rebuild twice from a frozen snapshot and compare canonical output digests.

requirements.statement: Use modular code, tests, error handling, logging, continuous integration, dependency management and input validation.
requirements.applicability: Production-ready harvesting and publication.
requirements.evaluation: Check tests, CI, pinned dependencies and safe logs.

uiTreatments: Link the published bundle to its source snapshot and evaluation report.
automatedChecks: Require byte-identical frozen rebuilds.
Scan build output and logs for secrets and local paths.

standards.title: Government Data Quality Framework

applicability.scope: Source metadata and generated bundle data
applicability.conditions: Assess fitness for purpose and retain metric definitions and denominators.
applicability.exclusions: Metadata cannot establish observation accuracy.

requirements.statement: Assess completeness, uniqueness, consistency, timeliness, validity and accuracy in relation to purpose.
requirements.applicability: Source lanes, reconciliation records and generated metadata.
requirements.evaluation: Automate bounded metadata tests for the first five; leave accuracy not-evidenced without independent or producer evidence.

uiTreatments: Show metric, denominator, method, date and evidence source for each quality result.
automatedChecks: Never infer observation accuracy from metadata completeness.

standards.title: ONS Classifications and Standards

applicability.scope: Records using an ONS, GSS, national or international classification
applicability.conditions: Preserve the named edition and source code.
applicability.exclusions: A text label is not sufficient evidence of classification identity.

requirements.statement: Preserve classification URI, name, version, definitions, codes and any documented deviation.
requirements.applicability: Records with classified dimensions, populations, activities, occupations, industries or geographies.
requirements.evaluation: Validate codes against the declared edition when an authoritative code list is available.

uiTreatments: Display classification name and edition; explain documented deviations.
automatedChecks: Reject an unversioned code match as proof of cross-edition equivalence.

standards.title: GSS Harmonised Standards and Guidance
standards.normativeStatus: Official GSS harmonisation standards and guidance

applicability.scope: Concepts, definitions, questions and outputs covered by a harmonised standard
applicability.conditions: Use only an evidenced mapping to a named standard and version.
applicability.exclusions: Do not infer harmonisation from similar wording.

requirements.statement: Preserve the harmonised concept or definition, version, implementation evidence, deviations and implications for comparison.
requirements.applicability: Statistical concepts with a source-published harmonisation statement.
requirements.evaluation: Require evidence before reporting harmonised alignment.

uiTreatments: Show harmonisation evidence and deviations in comparisons.
automatedChecks: Do not equate similar labels without an evidenced mapping.

standards.title: Using metadata to describe data assets in a data catalogue
standards.normativeStatus: Recommended open standard for UK government

applicability.scope: Public metadata for datasets, data services, distributions and catalogues
applicability.conditions: Use with the current UK metadata exchange model and DQV where quality measurements exist.
applicability.exclusions: Use GEMINI or INSPIRE metadata as well for applicable geospatial assets.

requirements.statement: Represent dataset, dataset series, distribution, data service and catalogue-record identity and relationships using DCAT 3.
requirements.applicability: All public bundle records as appropriate to record type.
requirements.evaluation: Validate JSON-LD expansion and profile cardinalities without claiming source-product compliance.

uiTreatments: Expose stable identifiers, publisher, versions, distributions and services.
automatedChecks: Run JSON Schema and SHACL profile checks against generated records.

standards.title: UK Cross-Government Metadata Exchange Model
standards.normativeStatus: UK application model for cross-government metadata exchange

applicability.scope: Dataset, data service and distribution exchange metadata
applicability.conditions: Follow published class and property cardinalities for the selected profile.
applicability.exclusions: Source absence is recorded rather than filled with guessed values.

requirements.statement: Preserve identifiers, descriptive metadata, responsibility, dates, access, licence, provenance and dataset-service-distribution relationships.
requirements.applicability: All mapped bundle assets.
requirements.evaluation: Validate required and recommended cardinalities and report missing evidence separately.

uiTreatments: Keep access rights and licence adjacent to download and service links.
automatedChecks: Validate profile cardinality, URI and ISO 8601 date forms.

standards.title: Data Catalog Vocabulary DCAT Version 3

applicability.scope: Semantic catalogue representation and export
applicability.conditions: Distinguish datasets, distributions, services, series and catalogue records.
applicability.exclusions: A distribution is not a duplicate dataset.

requirements.theme: Series, versions, services and qualified relations
requirements.statement: Use DCAT 3 version, series, checksum, distribution, service and qualified-relation terms according to their defined semantics.
requirements.applicability: Mapped bundle assets and JSON-LD export.
requirements.evaluation: Validate graph type and version-chain constraints.

uiTreatments: Render series and version history separately from download formats.
automatedChecks: Validate single-current acyclic version chains and resource types.

standards.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference

applicability.scope: Concepts, aliases, hierarchies and cross-scheme mappings
applicability.conditions: Mapping strength must be evidence-backed.
applicability.exclusions: Title similarity alone never establishes semantic identity.

requirements.statement: Use preferred, alternative and hidden labels, hierarchy and exact, close, broad, narrow or related mappings with their distinct meanings.
requirements.applicability: Topics, classifications, dimensions, options and cross-source concept links.
requirements.evaluation: Require explicit evidence for exactMatch and preserve close but non-equivalent alternatives.

uiTreatments: Keep close but non-equivalent datasets visible in Compare alternatives.
automatedChecks: Run SKOS label and mapping integrity checks.
Reject title-only exactMatch assertions.

standards.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology

applicability.scope: Acquisition, normalisation, derivation and producer-process provenance
applicability.conditions: Retain source and generated activity identities separately.
applicability.exclusions: The bundle build activity is not the upstream statistical production activity.

requirements.statement: Represent entities, activities and agents, including use, generation, derivation, primary sources, association and time.
requirements.applicability: Every harvested record and cross-source reconciliation claim.
requirements.evaluation: Require source URL, retrieval time, content digest and transformation identity.

uiTreatments: Provide a How produced view that distinguishes source and bundle transformations.
automatedChecks: Validate provenance graph references and content digests.

standards.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary
standards.normativeStatus: W3C Working Group Note, not a W3C Recommendation

applicability.scope: Machine-readable quality dimensions, metrics, measurements, annotations and policies
applicability.conditions: Each measurement must retain method, denominator and evidence.
applicability.exclusions: DQV use does not establish data quality or standards compliance.

requirements.statement: Represent quality dimensions, metrics, measurements, annotations and policies with explicit evidence.
requirements.applicability: Bundle evaluation and source-published quality measurements.
requirements.evaluation: Require metric definition, denominator, method, date and evidence source.

uiTreatments: Label measurements as bundle evaluation or producer evidence.
automatedChecks: Reject an unqualified score without metric and evidence metadata.

standards.title: RDF Data Cube Vocabulary

applicability.scope: Statistical structure metadata
applicability.conditions: Use for dataset structure, dimensions, measures, attributes, code lists and slices.
applicability.exclusions: Observation values are prohibited from the public metadata bundle.

requirements.statement: Preserve data-structure definitions, dimensions, measures, attributes and code-list references without materialising observations.
requirements.applicability: ONS Data API and Nomis structures where evidence exists.
requirements.evaluation: Validate structural references and reject observation values.

uiTreatments: Use structure metadata to configure a query, not to display statistical cells.
automatedChecks: Reject qb:Observation and equivalent observation payloads from published output.

standards.title: Statistical Data and Metadata eXchange 3.1
standards.normativeStatus: International statistical standard; SDMX is published as ISO 17369

applicability.scope: SDMX dataflows, structures, concepts, code lists, constraints and services
applicability.conditions: Preserve native identities and actual content constraints.
applicability.exclusions: Do not invent valid dimension combinations when constraints are unavailable.

requirements.statement: Preserve dataflow, DSD, concept scheme, code list, content constraint, metadata structure and service identities.
requirements.applicability: Nomis and other source surfaces that publish SDMX structures.
requirements.evaluation: Validate dimensions and options for the exact version and block known-impossible combinations.

uiTreatments: Generate MCP selection controls from the exact version's dimensions and constraints.
automatedChecks: Round-trip a selection plan without fetching observations.
Reject unknown dimensions, options and ambiguous geographies.

standards.title: Generic Statistical Business Process Model 5.2
standards.authority: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe

applicability.scope: Source-published statistical production process evidence
applicability.conditions: Map only activities that the source documents.
applicability.exclusions: Do not infer full process coverage from a methodology title.

requirements.statement: Classify documented production activities using the current GSBPM process model.
requirements.applicability: Methodology, process and quality evidence.
requirements.evaluation: Report evidenced process coverage without filling undocumented phases.

uiTreatments: Use a How produced process view with missing phases explicitly not-evidenced.
automatedChecks: Validate mapped process identifiers against GSBPM 5.2.

standards.title: Generic Statistical Information Model 2.0
standards.authority: United Nations Economic Commission for Europe

applicability.scope: Statistical information objects and their relationships
applicability.conditions: Use as a semantic crosswalk, preserving native source terms.
applicability.exclusions: A GSIM mapping does not replace the source identifier.

requirements.statement: Relate concepts, variables, populations, structures, products and processes using GSIM information classes.
requirements.applicability: Canonical OKF ontology mappings.
requirements.evaluation: Check mapping consistency while retaining source-native terminology.

uiTreatments: Use concept, population and represented-variable differences in comparisons.
automatedChecks: Validate canonical field-to-information-object mappings.

standards.title: DDI Common Core 1
standards.normativeStatus: DDI specification; DDI suite recognised as ISO/PAS 25955:2026

applicability.scope: Cross-domain statistical and research metadata concepts
applicability.conditions: Populate only source-evidenced entities and relationships.
applicability.exclusions: Do not require fields that the source does not expose.

requirements.statement: Preserve universe or population, concept, represented variable, value domain, instrument, collection, processing and quality statements when available.
requirements.applicability: Survey, census and administrative statistical products.
requirements.evaluation: Check field provenance and use not-evidenced rather than synthesising missing methodological metadata.

uiTreatments: Prioritise universe, concept and value-domain differences in dataset comparison.
automatedChecks: Require field-level provenance for DDI mappings.

standards.title: Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics

applicability.scope: High-level alignment of official-statistics evidence and presentation
applicability.conditions: Use for traceable reporting alignment, not producer certification.
applicability.exclusions: The bundle cannot determine professional independence or legal compliance.

requirements.theme: Impartiality, transparency, confidentiality and international comparability
requirements.statement: Preserve evidence relevant to impartial and equal access, source and method transparency, confidentiality, prevention of misuse and use of international standards.
requirements.applicability: Bundle-wide standards reporting.
requirements.evaluation: Map available evidence to principles without a pass or fail verdict.

uiTreatments: Link principle alignment to the exact evidence used.
automatedChecks: Prohibit certification language in principle coverage reports.

standards.title: United Nations National Quality Assurance Frameworks Manual for Official Statistics
standards.normativeStatus: UN Statistical Commission-adopted quality assurance framework

applicability.scope: Holistic evaluation taxonomy and self-assessment reporting
applicability.conditions: Use as a crosswalk for bundle evidence and source-specific QA.
applicability.exclusions: Do not claim that the bundle has assessed or certified the ONS institution.

requirements.statement: Cross-reference institutional, process and output quality evidence, including source-specific assurance.
requirements.applicability: Evaluation reporting and future maturity assessment.
requirements.evaluation: Report evidence coverage and applicability, not an institutional score.

uiTreatments: Keep UN NQAF as an evaluation crosswalk rather than a badge.
automatedChecks: Reject institutional certification claims.

standards.title: UK GEMINI 2.3 geospatial metadata profile
standards.normativeStatus: UK geospatial discovery metadata profile of ISO 19115

applicability.scope: Geospatial datasets and services with GEMINI or equivalent ISO metadata
applicability.conditions: Preserve the profile version and source validation result.
applicability.exclusions: A geographic statistical dimension alone does not imply GEMINI conformance.

requirements.statement: Preserve title, abstract, persistent identifier, resource locator, responsible organisation, lineage, constraints, dates, extent, quality, conformity, maintenance, series parent and CRS.
requirements.applicability: Open Geography and other spatial assets with official geospatial metadata.
requirements.evaluation: Validate supplied GEMINI 2.3 or ISO 19139 metadata and preserve the validation evidence.

uiTreatments: Show geography level, GSS code family, reference vintage, CRS and boundary variant next to the map.
automatedChecks: Validate bounding-box order and range.
Require geography code family and vintage where supplied.
Keep geometry payloads outside the metadata bundle.

standards.title: ISO 19115-1 Geographic information — Metadata — Part 1: Fundamentals

applicability.scope: Geographic information and services metadata
applicability.conditions: Use through an applicable implementation profile such as GEMINI where possible.
applicability.exclusions: The bundle does not reproduce the copyrighted standard text.

requirements.statement: Map identification, extent, lineage, constraints, quality, reference system, distribution and responsibility metadata where supplied.
requirements.applicability: Geospatial dataset and service records.
requirements.evaluation: Validate the selected public profile rather than claiming direct ISO certification.

uiTreatments: Provide a non-map textual presentation of spatial metadata.
automatedChecks: Validate mapped profile fields and source provenance.

standards.title: ISO 19157-1:2023 Geographic information — Data quality — Part 1: General requirements

applicability.scope: Geographic data quality descriptions, measures, evaluation and reporting
applicability.conditions: Use only source-published or independently measured quality evidence.
applicability.exclusions: A valid bounding box is not evidence of positional accuracy.

requirements.statement: Preserve quality component, measure, evaluation method, scope, result and report.
requirements.applicability: Geospatial records with geographic quality evidence.
requirements.evaluation: Require evidence and method for each geographic quality measurement.

uiTreatments: Keep spatial quality evidence separate from general metadata validity.
automatedChecks: Do not infer positional or thematic accuracy from metadata presence.

standards.title: Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data
standards.normativeStatus: W3C Recommendation and UK-recommended tabular metadata standard

applicability.scope: Actual tabular distributions
applicability.conditions: Map only columns, datatypes, keys and constraints exposed by the source.
applicability.exclusions: Do not download or publish the statistical rows.

requirements.statement: Describe table URL, dialect, columns, datatypes, titles, descriptions, keys and constraints where available.
requirements.applicability: CSV and other tabular distributions.
requirements.evaluation: Validate metadata structure without fetching or embedding data rows.

uiTreatments: Expose a schema preview without observation rows.
automatedChecks: Reject row data from the public bundle.

standards.title: GDS API technical and data standards

applicability.scope: Data services and API distributions
applicability.conditions: Link source-published endpoint descriptions and OpenAPI documents.
applicability.exclusions: Do not invent an endpoint contract that the provider does not publish.

requirements.statement: Preserve service endpoint, documentation, versioning, authentication class and machine-readable API description where published.
requirements.applicability: ONS and Nomis API data services.
requirements.evaluation: Validate credential-free public metadata URLs and link health.

uiTreatments: Show authentication requirements before generating an MCP plan.
automatedChecks: Reject credentials and secret query parameters.
Do not imply a generated MCP plan is an upstream API contract.

standards.title: DCAT Application Profile for data portals in Europe 3.0.1

applicability.scope: Optional European catalogue federation or export
applicability.conditions: Validate the export against the declared DCAT-AP release.
applicability.exclusions: DCAT-AP is not the primary UK authority for the canonical bundle model.

requirements.statement: Apply DCAT-AP class, property, cardinality and controlled-vocabulary constraints when producing a declared DCAT-AP export.
requirements.applicability: Only a generated DCAT-AP export.
requirements.evaluation: Run the release-specific SHACL validation and label the result as export-profile validation.

uiTreatments: Label DCAT-AP as an optional export profile.
automatedChecks: Do not use DCAT-AP alignment as a statistical-quality claim.
